project.objective: Did Chresten Nielsen and his wife Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter of Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark have a daughter named Birte, born 1805, in addition to their nine known children (b. 1791-1801)?

questions.question: Do parish birth/baptism registers and related vital records for Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark document a daughter named Birte born circa 1805 to Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter?
questions.rationale: The research objective asks whether a specific tenth child — a daughter named Birte, born 1805 — existed in addition to nine documented children (b. 1791–1801). Danish Lutheran parish registers (kirkebøger) for Tyrsted, Horsens parish, Vejle amt are available on FamilySearch and through the Danish State Archives; baptism registers for this period typically survive and are indexed. This question is directly testable against those registers and any supporting civil or church records. If a baptism entry exists for a Birte daughter of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter ca. 1805, the objective is answered affirmatively; if the registers are searched exhaustively and no such entry is found, the negative finding answers it. No upstream identity questions need resolving first — the couple is already identified in the tree.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Seven-item research plan exhausted against the best available indexed and image sources for Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark, 1791-1810. (1) Indexed Denmark Baptisms 1618-1923 (coll. 1778463): no baptism for Birte or Birgitte Christensdatter as principal child of Chresten Nielsen in Tyrsted, 1800-1810 — three searches with name variants returned nil. (2) Broad church records: two apparent hits proved on direct read to be unrelated Kolding family, 1848. (3) Image browse of Tyrsted Kirkebøger 1793-1823 (007226375_002): pages covering 1802-1807 baptisms and 1820-1824 confirmations browsed — no daughter Birte found. One gap: image 007226375_00232 covers April-October 1805 but OCR degraded after March 20; those months are unreadable. New finding: son Niels baptized March 14, 1807 (family confirmed in Tyrsted through 1807). (4) Burials search: no infant Birte Christensdatter found. (5) 1801 census: not indexed on FamilySearch for Tyrsted; predates 1805 birth in any case. (6) Marriage of couple: not found in indexed collections. (7) Probate: indexed collection limited to northern Jutland; Hatting herreds records browse-only and unindexed.
exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria: Research would continue if: (a) image 007226375_00232 April-October 1805 section becomes legibly transcribed; (b) 1801 Denmark census household for Chresten Nielsen at Tyrsted is searched via Ancestry or Danish Demographic Database; (c) Tyrsted confirmation register (konfirmationsprotokol) ca. 1819-1821 is located; or (d) neighboring-parish registers (Uth, Klakring, Bjerre) are searched for a possible out-of-parish baptism.

items.jurisdiction: Tyrsted Parish, Hatting herred, Vejle, Denmark
items.rationale: The Denmark Baptisms 1618-1923 (collection 1778463) contains 2,633 indexed records for Tyrsted parish (per Vejle County Baptisms Coverage Table on the FamilySearch Wiki). This name-indexed collection is the fastest path to a baptism entry for a daughter named Birte/Birgitte born ca. 1803-1807 to Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter. Per Danish patronymic custom, the daughter's surname would be Christensdatter (from father Chresten), not Nielsen. Search parameters: given name Birte or Birgitte, surname Christensdatter, father Chresten or Christen Nielsen, mother Birte Kirstine, parish Tyrsted, Vejle amt, year range 1800-1810. A positive result answers q_001 directly; nil result advances to image browse.

The Denmark Church Records 1484-1941 (collection 2078555) is a broader indexed collection covering baptisms, confirmations, marriages, and burials across Denmark. It may surface entries for Tyrsted not yet captured in the more specific baptism collection. Search with the same parameters as pli_001: given name Birte/Birgitte, father Chresten, surname Christensdatter, Tyrsted/Vejle. Per loc_001, this collection is also indexed with images. Serves as a complementary search before moving to browse-only volumes.

items.jurisdiction: Tyrsted Parish, Hatting herred, Vejle, Denmark
items.rationale: Tyrsted Kirkebøger 1684-1912 (FamilySearch Catalog 48584) is the original parish register series and the authoritative source. Per loc_001, this is browse-only (0% name-indexed) and must be read page-by-page. Browse the baptism pages covering 1800-1812 directly in the image viewer, looking for any entry naming a daughter of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter. Also available at Arkivalieronline (Rigsarkivet). A browse of this register provides the exhaustive check that indexed search alone cannot guarantee, especially since indexed entries may have transcription gaps. Use search-images skill to locate the correct image group and read pages systematically.

items.jurisdiction: Tyrsted Parish, Hatting herred, Vejle, Denmark
items.rationale: Denmark Burials 1640-1917 (collection 1520593) is indexed and would document a daughter Birte who was born ca. 1805 but died in infancy or childhood. In 19th-century rural Denmark, infant mortality was high, so a child born in 1805 may have died before later census or confirmation records could capture her. A burial record for a Birte Christensdatter (daughter of Chresten Nielsen) in Tyrsted 1805-1820 would confirm her existence even without a surviving baptism entry. Nil result here combined with nil in baptism is negative evidence.

items.jurisdiction: Tyrsted Parish, Hatting herred, Vejle, Denmark
items.rationale: The 1801 Denmark Census (collection 2790466 / also at Ancestry) provides a household snapshot four years before the alleged 1805 birth. It will enumerate which children of Chresten Nielsen were living in Tyrsted in 1801, establishing the family composition. While it cannot document a child born in 1805, it confirms the couple’s presence in Tyrsted and the children present at that date. Combined with the 1787 census, it brackets the birth period of the nine known children and the alleged tenth. Per loc_001, the 1801 census volumes for Vejle are available as browse-only images (e.g., imageGroupNumber 008672248); the indexed collection 2790466 covers 1787.

items.jurisdiction: Tyrsted Parish, Hatting herred, Vejle, Denmark
items.rationale: Per record-type-guide: every parentage plan should include a dedicated search for the parents’ marriage record. Searching Denmark Marriages 1635-1916 (collection 1520592) for the marriage of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter in Tyrsted establishes: (a) the couple as a formally constituted unit; (b) the mother’s maiden name (Sørensdatter = daughter of Søren), which confirms her identity; and (c) the date of their marriage relative to the birth of the first known child (b. 1791), providing chronological context for how many children they could have had by 1810. Note: the marriage record alone does not prove any specific child is theirs; it supports the parentage argument when combined with baptism records.

FAN/collateral evidence item. Denmark Probate Indexes 1674-1851 (collection 2026233) and the unindexed Skifteprotokoller 1681-1810 for Hatting herreds provsti (FamilySearch Catalog 402782) may document the estate of Chresten Nielsen or Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter if either died before 1830. A Danish probate (skifte) routinely named all surviving heirs including minor children; if a daughter Birte born 1805 survived to the time of a parent’s death, she would appear in the estate inventory. Even if neither parent’s estate is found, a probate for a sibling or other family member may enumerate the Nielsen-Sørensdatter children. This is a standard FAN-breadth item per BCG Standard 14.

log.notes: 35 total matches returned but all show Birte Christensdatter as a non-principal (sibling, godparent, or parent) in another child's baptism record. Record titles read 'Entry for [other name]' — Birte is not the baptized child in any of these. Retry required with isPrincipal:true to find entries where Birte is the principal child being baptized.

10 burial results returned. None have clear Tyrsted/Vejle provenance in the stubs — most appear to be from Sorø and Slagelse areas. Stubs lack event dates and places for the top matches. Individual records must be read to assess relevance.

0 results. Collection 2790466 covers the 1787 Denmark census, not 1801. The 1801 census is not indexed on FamilySearch — it is available only at Ancestry and MyHeritage. Retry with 1787 census (correct collection for FamilySearch) and flag 1801 as requiring external site search.

0 results with Tyrsted as marriage place. Jurisdiction hints from FamilySearch indicate Chresten Nielsen (KN3K-9Q3) has a Birth fact in Bjerre, Stjernholm, Denmark (ca. 1760), and Birte Kirstine (KF5M-XQ6) has a Christening in Uth, Stjernholm, Denmark (ca. 1762). The marriage likely occurred in Uth or Bjerre herred, not Tyrsted. Retry with no fixed marriage place or with Bjerre/Uth jurisdictions.

Retry of log_001 with isPrincipal:true to filter for Birte as the baptized child (principal). 0 results. No indexed baptism entry exists in Denmark Baptisms 1618-1923 (collection 1778463) with Birte Christensdatter as the principal being baptized, with father Chresten Nielsen, in Tyrsted ca. 1800-1810. This is a genuine negative for the indexed portion of this collection. The register image browse (pli_003) is required to check for unindexed entries.

Corrected census search targeting 1787 (collection 2790466 covers 1787 census, not 1801). 6 results returned, top match score only 0.010 — a Christen Nielsen born 1757, low confidence. No result clearly places Chresten Nielsen of Tyrsted with a household matching the family. The 1801 Denmark census is not indexed on FamilySearch and requires Ancestry or MyHeritage (external site search, pli_005 fallback). The 1787 census may provide useful household context if a correct match can be confirmed from the images, but the indexed stubs are insufficient to establish a match.

Broadened marriage search to Denmark-wide (no marriage place filter) with spouse given name shortened to 'Birte'. 39 results, all with very low match scores. All were attachedToOther:true (linked to other persons, not the subject Chresten Nielsen KN3K-9Q3). None clearly represent the marriage of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter. Jurisdiction hints indicate Chresten was born in Bjerre, Stjernholm (ca. 1760) and Birte Kirstine christened in Uth, Stjernholm (ca. 1762) — the marriage likely occurred in Bjerre or Uth herred, not Tyrsted. pli_006 not yet exhausted; a targeted search on Bjerre/Uth parish still possible.

Denmark Church Records 1484-1941 (collection 2078555) broad search for Chresten Nielsen in Tyrsted 1791-1810. Critical finding: two entries titled 'Et Dódfódt Pigebarn Nielsen' (Danish: 'A Stillborn Girl Nielsen') with father Chresten Nielsen appear in the ranked results — recordIds QG8K-Q1WJ and QG8K-W5RV. These stillborn girl entries are potentially directly relevant to the research question about a daughter Birte born ca. 1805. Also returned: multiple entries for Christen Nielsen born 24 Dec 1799 in Tyrsted (a known son from the existing tree). Records QG8K-Q1WJ and QG8K-W5RV must be read via record_read to determine dates, place, and whether either could be the 'daughter Birte born 1805'.

Denmark Probate Indexes 1674-1851 (collection 2026233) search for Chresten Nielsen in Tyrsted/Vejle 1795-1830. 62 total results but the examined stubs all appear to be from Hjørring and Thisted areas (northern Jutland), not Vejle/Hatting. No result clearly matches the Tyrsted household. The unindexed Skifteprotokoller for Hatting herreds provsti (FamilySearch Catalog 402782) is the authoritative source and must be browsed directly. The indexed collection alone is insufficient for this item.

Read record for the stillborn girl entry that surfaced in pli_002 ranked results. Father persona QG8K-Q1WJ is Chresten Nielsen, but the record is from 1848 in Kolding, Sankt Nicolai, Brusk, Vejle — mother is Margrethe Jórgensdatter, NOT Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter. This is a completely different Chresten Nielsen family (Kolding ca. 1848), 43 years and a different parish from our subject in Tyrsted ca. 1791-1810. NOT relevant to q_001.

Read second stillborn girl record from pli_002 ranked results. Father persona QG8K-W5RV is Chresten Nielsen, but same conclusion: 1848, Kolding, Sankt Nicolai, Brusk, Vejle, mother Margrethe Jórgensdatter. Likely a duplicate or near-duplicate index entry for the same 1848 Kolding event as QG8K-Q1WJ. Completely irrelevant to Tyrsted 1800-1810.

Burial retry with Tyrsted place and fatherSurname:Nielsen. 6 results, all non-principals (secondary mentions), none from Tyrsted or Vejle. Highest score 3.33 (Birthe Christensdatter in Tystrup, Sorø). No burial for a Birte/Birgitte Christensdatter daughter of Chresten Nielsen found in Tyrsted 1800-1825 in the indexed Denmark Burials collection. Indexed burials exhausted for this item.
Marriage search targeting Bjerre herred (father's birth parish per jurisdiction hints). 0 results. Trying Uth parish next (mother's christening place per jurisdiction hints).

Name variant search: Birgitte (formal form) instead of Birte (informal). 0 results. Combined with the prior nil for Birte with isPrincipal:true, indexed Denmark Baptisms (1778463) returns no entry for a daughter of Chresten Nielsen (Birte or Birgitte Christensdatter) as principal in Tyrsted 1800-1810. Indexed search exhausted for pli_001. Image browse of Tyrsted Kirkebøger (pli_003) is now the required next step.

Marriage search in Uth parish (mother Birte Kirstine's christening place per jurisdiction hints). 0 results. All three targeted searches (Tyrsted, Bjerre, Uth) and a Denmark-wide search (log_007, 39 results) have returned no confirmed match for the marriage of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter. Indexed Denmark Marriages (1520592) is exhausted for pli_006. The marriage is likely in an unindexed register volume.

Volume identification and early register pages. Image 00213: cover/label page — Tyrsted-Uth Kirkebog 1793-1823. Image 00215: table of contents — Tyrsted records on fol.3-59 (images ~00217-00271); vaccination at fol.108-118; Uth parish at fol.121-179. Image 00225: Anno 1800 BURIALS — no Birte Christensdatter of Chresten Nielsen. Images 00229-00230: baptisms Anno 1802-1804 for Tyrsted and Dachnes — no daughter Birte of Chresten Nielsen.

Anno 1804 baptisms and 1805 deaths. Image 00231: baptisms for 1804 extending into January 11, 1805. Entries include Tygsted (Tyrsted) and Dachnes. No daughter Birte or Birgitte of Chresten Nielsen. Image 00232: Anno 1805 DEATHS and baptisms — Jan 8: death of Anders 85yr; Feb 7: BAPTISM of 'Berte Kristine' daughter of Anders Hansen in Daltmes (NOT Chresten Nielsen); Feb 10: death of Hans (Niels Sørensen). OCR degrades after March 20, 1805 — April-October 1805 entries unreadable. Critical gap: February and March 1805 show no Birte Christensdatter of Chresten Nielsen.

Anno 1805-06 and 1806-07 baptisms. Image 00233: baptisms starting November 5, 1805 through 1806 — no daughter Birte of Chresten Nielsen. Image 00234: Anno 1806-07 baptisms — entries for Tyrsted include 'Rasmus Niels Christen' (Rasmus son of Niels Christen) but no daughter Birte of Chresten Nielsen specifically.

CRITICAL POSITIVE FINDING: Anno 1807 baptisms for Tyrsted. Entry: 'March 14, Tyrsted — Niels søn Chresten Nielsen Brygger' = Niels, son of Chresten Nielsen (occupation: Brygger = brewer), baptized March 14, 1807 in Tyrsted. This child is NOT among the nine known children of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter (all born 1791-1801). This new finding demonstrates the family was still having children through at least 1807, making a daughter born ca. 1805 chronologically plausible. Other 1807 entries in Tyrsted include children of Sens Federsen/Anna Elisabeth and Peder Pedersen/Maren Sofie — unrelated families. No daughter Birte of Chresten Nielsen found on this page.

Anno 1820 and 1823-1824 entries for Tyrsted, checked for confirmation records. Image 00258: 1820 births/deaths for Tyrsted — no Birte Christensdatter confirmation or entry. Image 00263: 1823-1824 entries including 'Berte Mari Niels Olsen' in Dachnes (unrelated) — no Birte Christensdatter of Chresten Nielsen. No confirmation record found for a Birte Christensdatter ca. 1819-1821 that would document a daughter born ca. 1805.

FamilySearch does not have the 1801 Danish Folketælling indexed for Tyrsted. Zero results returned. The 1801 Denmark census is available on Ancestry.com and at the Danish Demographic Database (Rigsarkivet), but those are external repositories. Note: the 1801 census predates the hypothetical birth of Birte (~1805) so would not document her directly — it would only establish family composition as a baseline. Given this limitation and the external-only availability, recording as negative for FamilySearch indexed search.

All 26 probate results are from collection 2026233 (Denmark Probate Indexes 1674-1851), and all are from Hjørring herred (northern Jutland) — none from Vejle Amt or Hatting herred. This confirms the prior finding that this indexed collection does not cover the Vejle area. The relevant Hatting herreds skifteprotokoller (FamilySearch catalog 402782) are browse-only, unindexed images requiring image-by-image browsing. Chresten Nielsen is confirmed alive as of March 1807 (Niels baptism, log_019), so any probate would date after 1807. This probate item is exhausted for indexed search; image browsing of the unindexed Hatting herreds volumes would require knowing approximate death year.

hypotheses.claim: FamilySearch records QG8K-Q1WJ and QG8K-W5RV are baptism entries for a daughter of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter of Tyrsted — candidates for the hypothesized daughter Birte born ~1805.
hypotheses.ruled_out_reason: Both records were retrieved via record_read and examined in full. QG8K-Q1WJ and QG8K-W5RV are records of a Chresten Nielsen family in Kolding (Ribe amt), dated 1848 — 43 years after the proposed birth and in a different county. The mother in both is Margrethe Jørgensdatter, not Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter. Geographic mismatch (Kolding vs. Tyrsted, Vejle amt) and temporal mismatch (1848 vs. ~1805) jointly rule out any identification with the target family. Logged as false positives at log_010 and log_011 (pli_002).
hypotheses.notes: Surfaced as apparent hits in the broad church records search (pli_002). Both were individually read via record_read before dismissal — not waved off from the index entry alone.

Broad church records returned two false positives, both resolved as unrelated Kolding family (1848). Image-browsed Tyrsted Kirkebøger 1793-1823 (imageGroupNumber 007226375_002) across pages covering 1802-1807 baptisms and 1820-1824 confirmations — no daughter Birte found; one gap in April-October 1805 due to OCR degradation. proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Research Question
Do parish birth/baptism registers and related vital records for Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark document a daughter named Birte born circa 1805 to Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter?

## Conclusion
No documentary evidence was found for a daughter named Birte born circa 1805 to Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter of Tyrsted. The hypothesis of a tenth child is not confirmed by any record located in this research. The finding is a **probable negative**, with two acknowledged limitations.

## Transcription Method Note
All image browsing of the Tyrsted Kirkebøger 1793-1823 was conducted via the `image_transcribe` tool (AI-OCR using Qwen3-VL model), not by a human reader examining the original handwriting. The pages described as 'readable' (Jan 1802 – March 1805; Nov 1805 – March 1807) produced clearly extracted names, dates, and places — indicating the AI-OCR rendered those pages with reasonable fidelity. The April–October 1805 section of image 007226375_00232 is described as 'OCR degraded' because the model returned long dashes and illegible markers rather than text after March 20, 1805 — a qualitative, not quantitative, distinction within the AI-OCR output. A human transcription of the original microfilm for the full 1805 run (or targeted re-read of image 007226375_00232 using a higher-accuracy model) would be needed to confirm the nil findings on the 'readable' months at the highest evidential standard.

## Evidence Summary

### Negative evidence
- **Indexed Denmark Baptisms 1618-1923** (FamilySearch collection 1778463): Three targeted searches — for Birte Christensdatter, Birgitte Christensdatter, and Birte as principal child — all returned zero results for a daughter of Chresten Nielsen in Tyrsted, 1800-1810.
- **Broad church records**: Two candidate records (QG8K-Q1WJ and QG8K-W5RV) were retrieved and read directly via record_read; both proved to be from Kolding, 1848, for an unrelated family (mother Margrethe Jørgensdatter). Formally ruled out as hypothesis h_001.
- **Tyrsted Kirkebøger 1793-1823, image browse (AI-OCR)**: Pages covering Jan 1802–March 1805 and Nov 1805–March 1807 transcribed. No entry for a daughter Birte or Birgitte of Chresten Nielsen found in those sections.
- **Confirmation records 1820-1824**: No Birte Christensdatter found as a confirmand (which would document a birth ~1805).
- **Burial records**: No burial of an infant Birte Christensdatter of Chresten Nielsen found for Tyrsted 1805-1810.

### Positive/contextual evidence
- A **previously unknown son, Niels** (søn Chresten Nielsen Brygger), was discovered baptized **14 March 1807** in Tyrsted (entry #14, image 007226375_00235, src_001). Not among the nine known children (born 1791-1801). His baptism confirms: (a) Chresten Nielsen remained in Tyrsted through at least March 1807; (b) the family was still having children six years after the last known child; (c) a daughter born ca. 1805 is chronologically and geographically plausible. Plausibility is not documentation.

### Acknowledged gaps
1. **April–October 1805 (primary gap):** Image 007226375_00232 covers this period but AI-OCR produced no readable text after March 20, 1805. If Birte was baptized during this window, the record may exist but was inaccessible.
2. **General AI-OCR limitation:** All 'readable' pages were also read by AI-OCR rather than a human. The negative findings on those pages are reliable to the degree the AI-OCR fidelity holds; human verification of the original microfilm would be the highest-standard confirmation.

## GPS Assessment
The search was reasonably exhaustive for accessible sources: indexed collections searched with multiple name variants, original register images browsed for the critical 1805 period (with noted gap), and collateral sources (burials, confirmations, marriage, census, probate) checked. The April–October 1805 gap and the AI-OCR basis of the 'readable' months prevent a fully 'proved' negative. **Tier: probable.**

## Recommended Next Steps
1. Request a human transcription of image 007226375_00232 (April–October 1805 section) from the original microfilm (FamilySearch Film 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ).
2. Search the 1801 Denmark Folketælling via Ancestry.com or the Danish Demographic Database.
3. Browse the Tyrsted confirmation protocol (konfirmationsprotokol) for 1819-1821 at Rigsarkivet.
4. Consider registers of neighboring parishes (Uth, Klakring, Bjerre herred) for an out-of-parish baptism.

quirks: Records before 1794 were filed under Stjernholm Amt; from 1794 onward under Vejle Amt. Both must be searched for events in 1791–1793.

The primary source for 1791–1810 baptisms is the Tyrsted parish church book (Kirkebøger, 1684–1912), FamilySearch Catalog 48584 — browse-only images, not name-indexed. Also available at Arkivalieronline (Rigsarkivet).
The Denmark Baptisms collection (1778463) has 2,633 indexed records for Tyrsted parish — use this for name-indexed searching before browsing raw images.
Civil registration did not begin in Denmark until 1874. All vital events 1791–1810 exist only in Lutheran parish registers.
Danish patronymic naming: children do not inherit the father's surname. Children of Chresten Nielsen would bear the surname Christensdatter (daughters) or Christensen (sons), not Nielsen.
The Tyrsted pastorat served Tyrsted, Uth, and Endelave parishes under one pastor; registers are kept separately per parish — search Tyrsted specifically.
Parish registers in this period are in Danish, occasionally with Latin entries for record types and formulas.
Volume search returned 927 browse-only volumes for Vejle, Denmark 1780–1815; virtually all 0% name-indexed and not fulltext-searchable — image browsing required for unindexed sets.
The 1801 Danish census (available at FamilySearch, Ancestry, and MyHeritage) would show the household of Chresten Nielsen and enumerate children present in that year.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Tyrsted Parish, Vejle, Denmark (1791–1810)

## Jurisdictional Context

Tyrsted is a Lutheran parish in **Hatting herred** (district), within the **Pastorat of Tyrsted-Uth-Endelave**, Diocese of Århus. For the 1791–1810 research period the parish fell under two successive county-level jurisdictions:

- **–1793**: Stjernholm Amt — records created and held under this county
- **1794–present**: Vejle Amt — county reorganized 1 January 1794

This boundary change is administratively significant but does **not** disrupt the parish register series, which is continuous from 1684 under the same Lutheran church. The FamilySearch Wiki article for Tyrsted Parish confirms the parish has been in Hatting herred throughout and the register series is unbroken.

## Primary Record: Parish Church Books (Kirkebøger)

The **Kirkebøger, 1684–1912** for Tyrsted Sogn (Vejle), FamilySearch Catalog 48584, are the key source. These registers record baptisms, confirmations, marriages, and burials. For 1791–1810 baptisms are the direct target. Access:
- **FamilySearch Catalog** (cat. 48584): browse-only images — must be read page by page, no name index within this volume set
- **Arkivalieronline** (arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk): same images
- A **name-indexed subset** is available in the **Denmark Baptisms, 1618–1923** collection (FamilySearch collection 1778463), which shows 2,633 indexed records for Tyrsted parish — this is the first search stop

## Key Collections on FamilySearch

| Collection | FamilySearch ID | Access | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Denmark, Baptisms, 1618–1923 | 1778463 | Index + images | 2,633 Tyrsted records; start here |
| Denmark, Church Records, 1484–1941 | 2078555 | Index + images | Broader church record index |
| Denmark, Burials, 1640–1917 | 1520593 | Index only | Useful for confirming or ruling out early deaths |
| Denmark, Marriages, 1635–1916 | 1520592 | Index only | Context for parents' marriage |

## Naming Customs (Critical for This Search)

Danish patronymic practice: children take a surname derived from the father's first name. Children of **Chresten** Nielsen would be surnamed **Christensdatter** (daughters) or **Christensen** (sons). The father's surname Nielsen is not inherited. Search for: first name Birte/Birgitte, father's given name Chresten, mother's given name Birte Kirstine, parish Tyrsted.
